focus: The shared gate and the four proven features' live-path pattern
noveltyJustification: First pass: the gate contract (FEATURES table, switch resolution, readiness probe, no-spawn property), all four proven live-path integrations, the auto-on provenance pattern, the stub-CLI test shape, and the cite-drift version-pin divergence are all new to this lineage.
keyQuestions: Q1: gate contract + four proven auto-on paths
answeredQuestions: Q1: What is the exact live-path contract behind `.skilled/skills/cli-classifier/shared/scripts/jev-features.mjs` (featureReady, JEV_FEATURE_<NAME>, auto-on with a stored credential), and how did each of the four proven features (cite-drift, injection screen hook, reviewer verdict fallback, D4 hallucination grader) earn its auto-on slot? What must a candidate feature demonstrate to pass that gate?
ruledOut: A gate change is needed to register candidates (FEATURES is data)
The gate costs a spawn when disabled (test asserts an empty stub log)

label: The gate registers exactly four features (cite-drift, injection-screen, verdict-fallback, hallucination-grader); the three candidates have no FEATURES entry, no JEV_FEATURE_ name and no live call site. Earning a live path means adding a FEATURES entry, a live call site that asks featureReady first, and docs; the gate itself needs no change.

The gate contract is switch-first then one bounded readiness probe: featureSwitch resolves master JEV_FEATURES, the feature env, then aliases (env wins per key over the hook-flags file; only 0/false/no/off switch off); jevReady walks PATH in-process then runs one bounded jev auth status --provider call (10s timeout, output discarded); featureReady composes them. A disabled feature never spawns, proven by the stub-CLI test asserting an empty log.

The four proven live paths share one integration shape: gate first, fail open to the pre-Jev behavior, never block. cite-drift gates runAdvise with featureSwitch plus a version-pinned private adviseGate; injection-screen returns done() when not ready; verdict-fallback resolves auto to jev or noop and records the gate reason; hallucination-grader resolves auto on the 5dim path only and hard-fails an explicit --grader jev without readiness.

The auto-on resolution records provenance: auto resolves once before any work to jev only when the gate is ready, otherwise noop, and the resolved grader plus gate reason are recorded so a shifted score is attributable; --grader noop restores the old score.

The test pattern for a gated feature is a stub-CLI fixture: a temp jev script recording argv, injected env/config, the full switch matrix (unset, master, feature, alias, config fallback, env-over-config), readiness pass/fail/no-CLI, a disabled-feature no-spawn proof, frozen FEATURES, and CommonJS reach with zero warnings. New feature tests can reuse this fixture shape and should target the candidate's own question constants, record shape and fallback behavior.

cite-drift diverges from the shared readiness check: it uses featureSwitch plus its own adviseGate that additionally requires an exact jev --version match; jevReady has no version pin. Two live-path shapes exist (shared readiness for injection-screen and both graders; version-pinned private readiness for cite-drift), and a version-sensitive candidate can follow the cite-drift precedent.
